novelty.justification: The core hypothesis is that an internal evaluation-awareness feature "causally raises the refusal-direction projection for harmful prompts," introducing a specific mechanistic coupling and an associated "eval-inflation gap" rather than merely a new safety-benchmark setting. Searches using "evaluation awareness activation steering refusal safety," "evaluation versus deployment refusal direction," and "situational awareness benchmark gaming LLM" identify the closest work as Hua et al., Probing and Steering Evaluation Awareness of Language Models (2025), which probes evaluation/deployment representations and notes that safety evaluations appear artificial, alongside Laine et al.'s SAD (2024) and Arditi et al.'s refusal-direction work. Moving from those works to testing whether evaluation awareness specifically gates the refusal mechanism is a substantive but natural integration of two established mechanistic lines, using standard contrastive directions and activation steering; I found no essentially equivalent prior study of this exact causal relationship, but the direction is predictable from existing evaluation-gaming concerns rather than a wholly new core paradigm.
